lines.text: Lead with London, then Lagos: that is where your show's listeners are strongest.
Aim the launch at people aged 25 to 34, as planned.
Build the positioning on storytelling and interviews: your listeners lean to it more than the listeners of rival shows do.
Name the subject, true crime, in the first line of the show description and in the first thirty seconds of the trailer.
Lead the key messages with storytelling, interviews and technology, the topics your listeners lean to that rival shows do not.
Pitch the show to press, newsletters and listeners in the company of Crime Junkie, Serial, My Favorite Murder with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark and Casefile True Crime.
names: My Favorite Murder with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark

lines.text: The core audience is people 25 to 29, then 30 to 34.
They also hear Casefile and The Long Con.
Plan London as a solid market: grow it with swaps and community events.
Plan Lagos as a smaller market: keep the spend small and lean on swaps and community.
Take the swap with Casefile forward: Casefile ranks 1 of 5 among the shows asked about for your show's listeners.
Offer a trailer swap or a guest slot to Casefile, The Long Con and Case Closed Weekly: they rank highest with your listeners.
Record the swaps before launch and release them in the first two weeks, so each show sends its listeners while the feed is new.
Open with guests who bring their own audience, and ask each to share the episode on the day it goes out.
Approach Glide Mobile and Fizz Cola in Lagos for an in-kind sponsorship or a co-promotion: they rank highest with your listeners.
Approach Glide Mobile and Fizz Cola in London for an in-kind sponsorship or a co-promotion: they rank highest with your listeners.
Send the platforms an editorial pitch six weeks out, and a short note with a link to the trailer to newsletters and press in your subject.
Publish a clip of the strongest minute of each episode with captions, and the full episodes on YouTube.
Plan a live recording or a listener meet-up in London, where your listeners are strongest.
Open a listener channel before the first episode goes out, and give its first members early access to the trailer.
Release weekly on one fixed day, and keep every episode in the same range of length so the feed feels reliable.
Lead on YouTube.
Lead on YouTube.
Hook one: open on the strongest image of Cold Case Lagos in the first two seconds.
Hook two: open on the question this release answers, as text on screen over the first shot.
Hook three: open on Lagos itself, with the name on screen.

Key art brief: one image, the title Cold Case Lagos and at most one line of text. Say what the image must show, what to avoid and where it will be seen, then hand it to a designer. Oraqul writes the brief; a person makes the art.
